div.l: And ellis receyue . thei were to blame .
It is full fayre . to be clepid ma dame .
And gon to vigiles . all bifore . /
And haue a mantell . ryalliche bore .
A Cook thei hadde . wtith hem for the nones .
To boyle chekenes . with the maribones
And pouder marchaunt . tart ⁊and galyngale .
Well knewe he . a draught of Londoūn ale .
He coude roste . boile ⁊and frie .
Maken mortreux . ⁊and well bake a pie .
But grete harme was it . as it thought me .
That on his schyne . a mormall had he .
For blank manger . that made he wiþ the beste .
A Schipman was there . wonyng fer bi weste .
For ought I wote . he was of dertemouthe .
He rood vp on a Rouncy . as he couthe .
In a gowne of faldyng . to the kne .
A dagger . hangyng on a lace had he .
A boute his nekke . vndyr his arme a doıı̄un .
The hote sonne . had made his hewe al broıı̄un .
And certeynly . he was a good felawe .
Full many a draught . of wyne had he drawe .
Fro Burdeux ward . while the Chapmen slepe .
Of nyce conscience . toke he no kepe .
Yf that he faught . ⁊and had the higher honde .
By water . he sente hem home . to euery londe .
But of his crafte . to reken well his tides .
His stremes . ⁊and his daungers hym besides .
His herberwe his mone . ⁊and his Lodemenage .
Ther was no such . fro hull vn to Cartage .
Hardy he was . ⁊and wys to vndyrtake .
With many a tempest . had his berde ben schake .
He knewe all the hauens . as thei were .
Fro Guthlonde . to the cape of fynystere .
And eủery crike in Brytayne . ⁊and in spayne .
pid was . the Mawdelayne .
n ther was . a doctour of phisik .
all the worlde . ne was ther / non hym lik .
e of phisik . ⁊and of surgerie .
For he was groūnded in astronomye .
He kepte his pacient . a full gret dele .
In houres . bi his magik naturele .
Well coude he fortune . the ascendent .
Of his ymages . for his pacient .
He knewe the cause . of euery maladye .
Were yt of hoot or colde . or moiste or drye .
And where engendrid . ⁊and of what humour . /
